item.title: Palestine's Eid dampened by consequences of war on livestock
item.description: Palestinians in Gaza facing another grim Eid holiday, which starts Tuesday evening. The livestock sector there has been destroyed by the war, and Israel isn't allowing the import of live animals, making the traditional animal sacrifice nearly impossible. Restrictions on border crossings also mean Palestinians are unable to perform the pilgrimage to Mecca.

item.title: Israel pounds Lebanon with fresh air strikes, vows to 'crush' Hezbollah
item.description: Israel intensified air strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon on Monday after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to “crush” Hezbollah, deepening fears of a wider regional conflict. The escalation comes despite an April ceasefire and as another round of US-Iran talks takes place in Doha in a bid to negotiate terms for a broader Middle East peace deal.

item.title: Middle East war live: Iran Revolutionary Guard official says renewed war with the US unlikely
item.description: The deputy political chief of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Wednesday that the possibility of a renewed war with the United States was "low'", but warned that Iran's armed forces were "lying in wait with full magazines" against any future attacks. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

item.title: Israel issues fresh evacuation orders in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
item.description: Israel has issued an evacuation order for residents in the southern Lebanese town of Nabatiyeh, warning of fresh strikes against Hezbollah, despite a ceasefire. It comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu promised to intensify attacks on Lebanon, following the killing of another Israeli soldier by a fibre optic drone sent by Hezbollah.

item.title: Israeli strikes kill dozens in southern Lebanon as Netanyahu expands ground campaign
item.description: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed 31 people and wounded 40 on Tuesday, Lebanon’s health ministry said, including at least four children and three women, as Israel said it was intensifying operations despite a truce with the Iran-backed group Hezbollah.

item.title: Israel strikes Lebanese village and calls up more troops in the region
item.description: The Israeli army has issued a fresh set of evacuation orders for 10 villages in Southern Lebanon as it prepares for a new round of military strikes. Israel and the militant group Hezbollah have been trading deadly fire despite a ceasefire. In fact, two far-right Israeli ministers are calling for more severe military action in Lebanon, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered an escalation of the offensive against Hezbollah.

item.title: Israeli defence ministry says it killed new Hamas military leader in Gaza
item.description: Israel's defence ministry said Wednesday they had targeted and killed the new leader of Hamas' military wing, Mohammed Odeh, during air strikes in Gaza City less than two weeks after killing his predecessor. Defence Minister Israel Katz called him “one of the architects” of the October 7 attacks that triggered over two years of war in Gaza.

item.title: Iran says US violated ceasefire with strikes near Hormuz
item.description: Iran accused the United States on Tuesday of breaching a fragile ceasefire with strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, threatening efforts to end nearly seven weeks of conflict. Washington said the attacks were defensive, targeting missile sites and vessels allegedly laying mines.

item.title: Iran looking to 'buy time to rebuild its military' amid talks to end war
item.description: Iran accused the United States of breaching their ceasefire and warned it was ready to retaliate after overnight US strikes targeting Iranian missile sites and mine-laying boats. Despite the strikes, the US is adamant that a deal was within reach, and a top Iranian official delegation in Qatar says it is finalising a 14-point framework for a deal to end the war. FRANCE 24's Philip Turle looks at where talks are stalling.

item.title: 'How to shoot down an F-18': Videos show Iran militia members training to use anti-aircraft missiles
item.description: Iran’s military forces are preparing for a potential new round of US-Israeli attacks by deploying more man-portable air defence systems, or MANPADS, drawing on lessons from the recent war and the downing of multiple US and Israeli aircraft. FRANCE 24 obtained documents and videos revealing mass training by the Revolutionary Guards for members of the Basij, the IRGC’s paramilitary force, on how to fire MANPADS.
